No out-of-sample validation was run (_validation: NOT RUN), so the statistics describe only in-sample fit and I have no way to assess whether the tail shape and Sortino generalize

reasons: Single-month concentration: 2025-04 contributes 3770 of total P&L ≈ 8489, i.e. ~44% of all profit from one month out of 18; removing that month leaves roughly half the result.

Single-hour concentration: hour 17 UTC alone contributes 2256 (~27% of total P&L), and hours 14-17 UTC together contribute 5129 (~60% of total P&L), so the result is dominated by one slice of the trading day.

Top-heavy session distribution: profit_concentration_top5pct = 0.47, i.e. the top 5% of sessions deliver roughly half of all profit, and 225 of 384 sessions with exposure are losing sessions (~59% losing rate).

The by-month series is highly erratic with 7 of 18 months negative (some deeply, e.g. -708 in 2025-01 and -310 in 2024-10) and one outlier month driving nearly half the total; this is the signature of a strategy whose P&L is carried by a few events rather than broadly distributed edge.
auditors.confidence_note: Without per-trade records, per-session P&L distribution beyond the summary stats, or any out-of-sample run, I cannot say whether this concentration is a structural feature of the strategy or an artifact of the training window, but the in-sample concentration is material enough to distrust the headline result on its own.
